data.function: P2 report: USB protection: no survivor
data.ruling: The refutation stands. Two of the figure's stated numbers are false for parts the same P2 return lists as found and dropped. (1) The figure says "Passive clamps stand off 5.5 V and break down at 6.3 V or more". The P2 drop list includes USBLC6-2SC6 (C7519) and USBLC6-2P6 (C15999). ST's USBLC6-2 datasheet, Table 2, gives IRM at VRM = 5.25 V and VBR between VBUS and GND at 6 V min at IR = 1 mA. The P2 drop reason for the USBLC6 row itself cites VRM 5.25 V. (2) The figure says "every D+/D- OVP switch found trips at 3.61 to 4.7 V or gives no limits". The P2 drop list includes TS5USBC400/402 and TS5USBC410/412. TI gives VOVP_TH as 4.5 min, 4.8 typ, 5.2 max V for the TS5USBC400 and 4.4 min, 4.8 typ, 5.2 max V for the TS5USBC41x, so switches found trip at up to 5.2 V. The corrected wording: clamps stand off 5.25 to 5.5 V and break down at 6 V min or more; OVP switches trip between 3.61 V min and 5.2 V max. The conclusion does not change: no part found meets V12's 3.63 V steady limit at USB_DP and USB_DM, and none covers VBUS, D+, D-, CC1 and CC2 together. A 5.25 V stand-off still passes steady voltages above 3.63 V, and a 4.4 to 4.5 V minimum trip point still passes them. The figure goes forward with the corrected numbers and the same "no survivor" conclusion. Scope is function: the defect is in how this function's report states requirement-related values, not in any part's lifecycle, maker or LCSC identity.
data.evidence: usblc6-2.pdf (SHA-256 bc30154f310cd631043214ed52571daefe04270587ec55072d49a23bd18b9068), Table 2 Electrical characteristics (Tamb = 25 C): 'IRM Leakage current VRM = 5.25 V ... 10 typ 150 max nA'; 'VBR Breakdown voltage between VBUS and GND, IR = 1 mA, 6 min V'. ts5usbc400.pdf (SHA-256 2b5fab2b5fd5ce63700e7594ccf4149998631b8d5abd3fb0aef4d3b9900b05a1), Electrical Characteristics, Protection: 'VOVP_TH OVP positive threshold 4.5 / 4.8 / 5.2 V' (min/typ/max); VOVP_HYST 75 / 230 / 425 mV. ts5usbc41.pdf (SHA-256 fc58583e7ec07f9cb7fd68bc8bb0bb749bfa683bcd460b91cd4f6d140a68fdde), Protection: 'VOVP_TH OVP positive threshold 4.4 / 4.8 / 5.2 V'; VOVP_HYST 125 / 250 / 440 mV. The P2 return /home/claude/rcbench-research/round1/scratch/FU-A4/P2-R1/return.json lists both families among the USB protection drops: 'USBLC6-2SC6 (C7519), USBLC6-2P6 (C15999), ...' with reason '(USBLC6 VRM 5.25 V, FU-A1 P2 reading)', and 'TS5USBC400/402 (C2879627, C2863308, C2872261, C2150844), TS5USBC410/412 (C2859808, C2150855, C2150853, C54561922)' with reason 'VOVP_TH 4.4 to 4.5 V min'. Both parts still fail V12 (3.63 V steady), so the no-survivor conclusion holds. The verifier's other confirmations (VBUS54CV-HSF, TPD6E05U06, TPD4S311 and TPD6S300A, USB 2.0 Table 7-7) are not disputed by this ruling and were not re-read; the refutation already holds on the two numbers above.
